_what: THE AUTHORITATIVE pool watchlist for the Helius POOL webhook.
_why_git: It lived only in Supabase, and when the database stopped answering at 2026-09-23 04:06Z the list became unreadable AND unrecoverable: the webhook could not be restored because the only copy of what to watch was behind the outage. CLAUDE.md already settled this ('State store is git. Supabase is a write-only mirror') and the receiver violated it. Git is now the source; Supabase is a mirror written best-effort and never read as truth.

_budget._delivery_multiplier_note: PRE-COMMITTED HEADROOM, and it is the honest handling of a thing we have NOT established. Delivered events per second were 1.4x to 297x the chain transaction rate across an 88 second window with single-digit per-pool counts, so the ratio is an observation and not a rate. Until a real measurement exists, the admitted set must satisfy chain_total * 5 <= budget_per_sec. That is why 6 of 11 budget-passing pools are held back rather than registered.
_budget._probe_caveat: Standing rule 13: a 600 second window on a pool that fires a few times an hour is a weak estimate, and two pools measured exactly 0.0000/sec, which means no transaction in the window rather than a proven silent pool.

_selection_rule: Ascending measured chain rate, admitting pools until chain_total * delivery_multiplier_assumed would exceed budget_per_sec. Any pool above addr_max_per_sec is refused outright, and any pool whose rate could not be established is refused (unknown is not zero).
